summary: Mirny Airport (MJZ/UERR) is a regional airport serving the city of Mirny in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), one of Russia's most remote diamond-mining centers. The airport provides a vital air link to this subarctic outpost, where winter temperatures regularly plunge below -40°C. It primarily handles domestic flights connecting Mirny to hubs like Yakutsk and Moscow, supporting both passenger travel and the region's lucrative diamond industry.
faqs:
Q: What is the best time of year to fly into Mirny Airport?
A: Summer (June-August) offers the mildest weather and most reliable flight schedules, as extreme winter cold in Yakutia can sometimes cause delays or cancellations.

Q: Are there international flights from MJZ?
A: No, Mirny Airport only operates domestic flights, primarily to Yakutsk and Moscow, with possible seasonal services to other Russian cities.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a medium-sized regional airport, it offers basic passenger amenities including a small terminal, limited food and beverage options, and standard check-in services, but no extensive retail or lounge facilities.

Q: How reliable are flights in winter?
A: Flights can occasionally be disrupted by severe cold, snowstorms, or low visibility common to the Siberian interior, so building buffer time into travel plans is advisable.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a few kilometers from Mirny's city center, making taxi the fastest and most common transfer option, typically taking only 10-15 minutes. There is no rail service to Mirny, so most arrivals and departures rely on the airport. Booking a taxi in advance through your hotel is recommended, as app-based services are limited in this remote region.
local_tip: If you have a long layover or extra time, ask your hotel or guide about a visit to the viewing platform overlooking the famous Mir diamond mine—one of the largest open-pit mines
